articles.title: HelloFresh workers claim physical abuse and denied bathroom breaks in class action suit
articles.summary:
The meal kit delivery service denies the allegations, saying it found claims to be ‘entirely without merit’

Workers at a HelloFresh facility in Newark,

blocks.text: Workers at a HelloFresh facility in Newark, New Jersey have claimed in court documents that they were verbally and physically abused and denied regular bathroom breaks, with one former worker telling the Guardian he experienced incontinence issues as a result.

The newly proposed amended complaint comes in a class action lawsuit first filed in August 2024 against the food prep service giant and staffing agencies. A New Jersey state court judge is expected to review the amended complaint in a hearing scheduled for 23 October.

In the civil lawsuit, workers allege HelloFresh and temp staff managers took ID badges from temp workers that are required to be able to leave the facility, repeatedly threatened to call ICE and immigration authorities on workers, subjected workers to physical and verbal abuse, sexually harassed Hispanic female employees, and discriminated against the temp workforce that consisted primarily of Hispanic workers in violation of New Jersey’s anti-discrimination laws.
A spokesperson for HelloFresh denied all allegations in the lawsuit.

“Upon learning of these allegations, which date from 2023 and years prior, we conducted a thorough internal investigation and found these claims to be entirely without merit. We vehemently denied these allegations when this lawsuit was filed over two years ago, and we continue to vehemently deny them today,” the spokesperson said in an email.
In a motion to dismiss, filed by HelloFresh in April 2025, the subscription-based meal kit delivery service denied the allegations in the lawsuit.
Action Staffing, On Target Staffing and ProStaff Workforce Solutions did not respond to multiple requests for comment but have moved to dismiss the lawsuit.

The lawsuit alleges HelloFresh assigned its Hispanic workers “the hardest work”, and that supervisors consistently made racist, abusive remarks to workers and berated them for speaking Spanish rather than English. The suit claims supervisors enforced a no-cellphone policy for Hispanic workers, while not enforcing it for others.

Luis Penafiel, a former temp worker at the HelloFresh distribution center in Newark, New Jersey from November 2021 to August 2023, and a plaintiff in the lawsuit claims that the working conditions began to deteriorate shortly after he was hired. “We started to realize that because we were Latinos, we were being forced to do all these kinds of duties. We started noting the discrimination,” he said.
“We were afraid of punishment for complaining,” said Penafiel. “We want the authorities to listen to us and to realize the conditions that people are working under at these places.”
According to the complaint, workers also alleged Hispanic workers were required to use a sign-out system in order to use the bathroom and that management policed the time they spent in the bathroom.

“There were many times I had to hold it for hours because they would note down the time you went in,” Penafiel said. “I had to go to the clinic to a urologist because I started experiencing incontinence, as I had to hold it for a long time and ended up getting infections.”

The lawsuit claimed non-Hispanic workers were allowed to use the bathroom whenever they wanted and for however long, often with the temp workers expected to fill in on work lines for direct hires when they took longer breaks or were using the bathroom.

“On several occasions, a HelloFresh manager menaced Hispanic workers with a baseball bat to limit their time in the bathroom and force them to return to work on HelloFresh’s production line,” the complaint alleges. “HelloFresh’s bathroom policy was so restrictive that several Hispanic workers were forced to urinate on themselves and continue to work because their supervisors denied them permission to use the bathroom.”

It added, “defendants’ bathroom policies were so restrictive that at least one member of the Hispanic Employee Class brought multiple pairs of underwear and fresh clothes to work because she was forced to urinate on herself on several occasions.”

The complaint alleges instances of workers grabbing female employees’ body parts, having managers show workers pornography and photos of their genitalia, using loaves of bread and cucumbers to simulate sex acts, and regularly propositioning female workers for sex.

“HelloFresh supervisors physically assaulted and battered several Hispanic employees during their employment at HelloFresh,” the lawsuit alleges, arguing the alleged assaults were done in view of other Hispanic employees with the intent of inducing fear of not following supervisors’ directives.

The lawsuit described the alleged assaults as managers “physically beating workers”, “putting their hands around workers’ necks” and “screaming in workers’ ears”. The lawsuit also claimed workers were denied medical treatment for injuries sustained on the job.

“When people would raise complaints about what they were suffering, what supervisors were doing, they were bounced back and forth between HelloFresh and the staffing agencies with very little resolution, so there was really no place for people to go with these complaints,” said Lauren Herman, an attorney with Make the Road New Jersey and one of the plaintiff’s attorneys in the lawsuit.

“I think this lawsuit really illustrates what happens when you have effectively a two-tier labor force in the economy where we have the kind of aggressive immigration enforcement that’s happening right now that leaves people feeling so vulnerable that employers can hold their immigration status over their heads in this way and use that as a tool to exploit them,” said Michael Scimone, a partner at Outten and Golden representing the workers in the lawsuit.
In court filings, the staffing agencies claimed HelloFresh offered direct employment to all workers, which the plaintiffs’ lawsuit disputes.

Target Staffing’s attorneys argued in its motion to dismiss that the workers falsified their immigration documents and would not clear HelloFresh’s verification system. They also claimed no workers ever complained about the work environment at HelloFresh.

The requests from each staffing agency to dismiss claims alleging violation of the New Jersey Human Trafficking Prevention, Protection, and Treatment Act were granted, though the judge allowed the plaintiffs to file an amended complaint to specify individually named plaintiffs or defendants.

In December 2024, the US Department of Labor announced an investigation into a different staffing agency at a HelloFresh facility in Illinois over allegations that migrant children were working at the facility. HelloFresh noted it terminated its relationship with the agency upon learning about the allegations.

“Our frontline workforce is the foundation of our company, and ensuring a safe, fair, and respectful workplace is our highest priority,” HelloFresh said in an email. “HelloFresh maintains robust anti-discrimination and anti-harassment policies governed by our Employee Handbook and Global Code of Ethics. They are backed by mandatory training and multiple reporting channels, including a 24/7 confidential hotline for anonymous complaints. We take every concern seriously and remain fully dedicated to upholding a culture of integrity and accountability.”

articles.title: Senate panel endorses DENR's P28-B budget for 2027
articles.summary: A Senate Finance subcommittee on Monday endorsed to the plenary the proposed P28.04-billion budget of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and its attached agencies for 2027.

blocks.text: Published October 19, 2026 6:58pm
A Senate Finance subcommittee on Monday endorsed to the plenary the proposed P28.04-billion budget of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and its attached agencies for 2027.
In his presentation, DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna said P20.62 billion of the proposed budget would go to the department’s central office, staff bureaus, regional offices and other smaller offices.

The remaining funds would be allocated as follows: P3.10 billion for the Environmental Management Bureau (EMB), P1.98 billion for the National Mapping and Resource Information Authority (NAMRIA), P1.89 billion for the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB), P284.35 million for the National Water Resources Board (NWRB) and P149.3 million for the Palawan Council for Sustainable Development Staff (PCSDS).

Aside from the DENR’s proposed programs and projects for next year, Sen. Risa Hontiveros, who led the budget hearing, urged the department to prioritize preparedness and emergency response measures against the threat of a super El Niño.

“Hindi pwedeng taumbayan lang ang mag-aadjust (the public shouldn’t be the only ones expected to adjust). DENR must step up to a historic challenge. It will be a critical and leading agency in the government’s response to this looming risk of widespread drought," Hontiveros said.
"The agency’s work will have real, tangible implications for the economy, health and daily living conditions of millions,” she added.
Hontiveros stressed that the DENR’s budget should adequately fund preparations and emergency response measures to mitigate the impact of the looming drought on Filipinos.
“Filipino people expect agility in the response and fitness for purpose of the budgets of frontline agencies such as the DENR. Its budget should reflect this," she said.
"Dapat buhusan ng pondo ang paghahanda at emergency response sa paparating na tagtuyot para maibsan ang dagok nito sa bawat Pilipino,” Hontiveros added.
(Funds must be allocated for preparations and emergency response to the looming drought to mitigate its impact on every Filipino.)

Hontiveros also called for funding for small water impoundment systems to collect and store rainwater for use during droughts. She said available technologies, such as atmospheric water stations developed by the Local Water Utilities Administration, should also be tapped to identify alternative sources of potable water.
Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano, meanwhile, called for stronger environmental education in elementary and high school curricula.

He said the DENR should work closely with the Department of Education (DepEd) and the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) to ensure that practical lessons on ecology and conservation are integrated into school curricula.

Sen. Pia Cayetano likewise urged the DENR to collaborate with education agencies to ensure that environmental education addresses the specific needs of coastal and mountainous communities.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: From delivery driver to global fame: A Korean writer's journey
articles.summary: You Yeong-Gwang's The Rainfall Market tells the story of a mysterious, hidden shop that only opens when it rains. For a debut novel by an unknown author, it was a massive success.

image.caption: The book was a massive success, securing publication in 15 languages, including English, German, Spanish and ChineseImage: ClayHouse/Michael Joseph/Ace

blocks.text: For ten years, publishers rejected You Yeong-Gwang's book. Yet before it was even printed in South Korea, the once-abandoned manuscript had international publishers flocking to secure translation rights.

"I'm so grateful that the book has now been published in more than 20 countries. Even more astonishingly, it also appeared on the Der Spiegel bestseller list in Germany," he told DW while attending the 2026 Frankfurt Book Fair.
For a debut novel by an unknown author, it was a massive success, securing publication in 15 languages, including English, German, Spanish and traditional Chinese.

The Rainfall Market tells the story of a mysterious, hidden shop that only opens when it rains. In the shop, visitors can exchange their deepest unhappiness for a ticket to a brand-new destiny. The plot revolves around Serin, a disheartened young girl who stumbles into the marketplace run by whimsical spirits, finding a warm, comforting space.
"In fact, Serin's story is my story," author You said. "For a long time, I even wondered how wonderful it would be if I could sell my unhappiness and use the money to buy happiness."
While writing the book, he was going through a difficult time himself.
"I had to care for my mother, who had been ill for a long time, and I had also been responsible for supporting my family financially for many years. Life felt incredibly heavy," he reflected.

"But when I was writing, I could immerse myself in the world of the story and, even if only for a short while, forget about those circumstances. That's why writing made me so happy. I truly enjoyed it."
On the creation of The Rainfall Market
The idea of rain is inspired by his own life. "At that time, my circumstances felt as though it were raining constantly," You said.

blocks.caption: You Yeong-gwang, author of 'The Rainfall Market'Image: ClayHouse

blocks.text: The story draws heavily on traditional Korean folklore, serving as a quintessential "healing fiction" tale in which its young protagonist must weigh the true cost of seemingly perfect lives.
"When I was writing, I wasn't consciously trying to write healing fiction. At the time, I didn't even really know that such a label existed."

He initially planned to publish a book independently and started crowdfunding. But as the funding failed, he used all his savings and printed 200 copies, which bookstores refused to take. In a month, he only sold five copies. "I thought that's it. I really have to give up now.”

"At the time, I had undergone eye surgery and due to complications, I couldn't see, so I started working at a call center, where I could work using my voice." You said. "During the week, I worked at a call center, and on weekends I went to a computer academy. I learned how to make books on my own for a few years."
He then taught himself how to use the software needed to create books on his own.

While running one of the crowdfunding campaigns, he started working as a food delivery rider. "The round trip between my home and the area where I delivered food took about four hours each day. So I wrote on my phone's memo app while traveling on the subway."

"Even when I was going through very difficult circumstances, I was able to keep writing because the moments when I was writing were so joyful. For a little while, I could forget about the difficult situation I was in," You explained.
Finally a breakthrough
"I gathered those pieces of writing together and launched what I intended to be my final crowdfunding campaign," he said.
The campaign was intended to fund the publication of The Rainfall Market.
"To my amazement, the campaign succeeded, and I was able to publish the book commercially for the first time," he said.
How K-pop pushes appetite for Korean ramyun noodles
Following the crowdfunding success, the novel was acquired by Clayhouse, a prominent South Korean publishing company.
Before it was even published, he had received offers from publishers in five countries and signed international publishing contracts.
And in the first month after publication, the book sold 30,000 copies across all formats, ranking as the bestselling e-book and third-bestselling physical book.
"I still find it hard to believe that all of this has happened and that I'm here at the Frankfurt Book Fair. I'm incredibly grateful and happy," said You.
A new horizon for Hallyu, or the 'Korean Wave': K-Comfort Fiction
Korea's newest soft power is K-literature, which sold about 1.2 million translated copies abroad in 2025 for the second consecutive year.
And You's book belongs to a trending genre called Korean comfort fiction.
"When readers closed the book, I wanted them to feel a little warmth in their hearts," he said.

Although Korean literature was first known for darker, more pragmatic books about societal realities, K-comfort fiction is the child of South Korea's pressure-cooker modern society. It offers an answer to the human need for escapism and a transient antidote to the reality of a hyper-competitive education system, brutal job market, and intense corporate pressure.

"When I was writing, I was going through a very difficult time myself, and I wished someone would comfort me. So, I thought, why don't I try reading something like that myself? Why don't I write something that can comfort me?" You wondered.

With burnout on the rise globally, more readers are seeking soul-soothing literature with exhausted protagonists they can relate to. Usually without a need to defeat a villain, the stories follow protagonists with a deep desire for rest, community and emotional repair.

The whimsical fiction aspect is the missing element allowing them to step away from reality. The genre originally gained traction through indie productions, online crowdfunding and endorsements from high-profile K-pop artists.
How South Korea is cashing in on 'KPop Demon Hunters'

Despite the Korean context, this style of storytelling quickly went global, capturing different international audiences, including those already familiar with cozy K-dramas or those simply looking for a gentle refuge from the anxieties of the modern world.

Last year, the bestselling Korean novel abroad was Welcome to the Hyunam-dong Bookshop, according to the Literature Translation Institute of Korea. This book also belongs to the same genre as The Rainfall Market.

While readers embrace the genre, critics view it with literary skepticism. They point out that it relies heavily on a predictable, repetitive formula, often built around a single magical space, with simplistic prose and low-stakes conflicts that prioritize cozy vibes over deep character development.

Reviewing The Rainfall Market for the Korea Times, Peter Juhl, a literary critic, described healing fiction as light, feel-good stories and argued the boom reflects a deliberate effort to write global novels for international markets.
On his future aspirations and message to readers

"Of course, I'm happy that my book is receiving so much love and that I'm able to write. But more than anything, I hope my mother gets better and regains her health," he said after mentioning that his mother underwent surgery a week before his arrival at the book fair.
Beyond the book itself, people seem to relate to and appreciate the story of his own life.

"If I have the opportunity, I'd like to share more stories about hope and dreams with people who are going through circumstances similar to mine," said You. "If my story can help one person even a little, in any way, I don't think anything could make me happier."

articles.title: Champi now a super typhoon again ahead of entry into PAR
articles.summary: The trough or extension of Super Typhoon Champi may already trigger scattered rain and thunderstorms in Catanduanes, Northern Samar, and Eastern Samar, says PAGASA on Monday afternoon, October 19

blocks.text: CHAMPI. Satellite image of Super Typhoon Champi outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility as of October 19, 2026, 4 pm.
PAGASA
The trough or extension of Super Typhoon Champi may already trigger scattered rain and thunderstorms in Catanduanes, Northern Samar, and Eastern Samar, says PAGASA on Monday afternoon, October 19

items: Champi re-intensified into a super typhoon outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility, with maximum sustained winds of 185 km/h.
The super typhoon remains on track to enter PAR by Tuesday, October 20.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Champi re-intensified into a super typhoon on Monday afternoon, October 19, ahead of its expected entry into the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR).

Champi’s maximum sustained winds increased from 175 kilometers per hour to 185 km/h, said the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) in an advisory issued at 5 pm on Monday. Its gustiness is now up to 230 km/h from the previous 215 km/h.
The super typhoon was located 1,515 kilometers east of southeastern Luzon as of 4 pm, moving west northwest at a slightly slower 15 km/h from 20 km/h.
It is still projected to enter PAR by Tuesday morning or early afternoon, October 20. Upon entry, it will be given the local name Rosal.

PAGASA said Champi will continue to move west northwest until Wednesday, October 21, before moving generally northwest starting Thursday, October 22. It is likely to stay over the Philippine Sea, where it could strengthen further before gradually weakening Thursday onwards.

Even before Champi enters PAR, its trough or extension may already trigger scattered rain and thunderstorms in Catanduanes, Northern Samar, and Eastern Samar in the coming hours. Flash floods and landslides are possible.

The super typhoon could be closest to the Philippines’ northernmost province of Batanes on Friday, October 23. It is expected to bring heavy rain to extreme Northern Luzon, or the Batanes-Babuyan Islands area, even though it is unlikely to make landfall.

Tropical cyclone wind signals might also be raised for the northern and eastern portions of Northern Luzon and even parts of Bicol as early as Monday evening or Tuesday morning. The weather bureau’s latest forecast shows Signal No. 2 or 3 could be the highest, while Signal No. 4 is no longer seen as a possibility.
PAGASA added that most parts of Luzon and the Visayas, as well as portions of Mindanao, are likely to experience gusty conditions beginning Wednesday.
As for coastal conditions, moderate to rough waters are expected in the northern and eastern seaboards of Luzon and the eastern seaboards of the Visayas and Mindanao on Tuesday.
Starting Wednesday, very rough, high, or very high waters may affect the northern and eastern seaboards of Luzon.
Champi may exit PAR by Saturday, October 24.

items: Sandiganbayan suspends Marcoleta as senator over plunder case
News Reflection: Bongbong Marcos didn’t get what he wanted

blocks.text: Aside from the trough of the super typhoon, other sources of rain in the coming hours include the intertropical convergence zone (ITCZ) and the easterlies.
The ITCZ is a belt near the equator where the trade winds of the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere meet, while the easterlies are warm winds from the Pacific Ocean.

Scattered rain and thunderstorms will persist in the Zamboanga Peninsula and Palawan due to the ITCZ, while isolated rain showers or thunderstorms may hit Cagayan Valley, the Cordillera Administrative Region, and the Ilocos Region because of the easterlies.
The Philippines is currently in a transition period to the northeast monsoon or amihan, following the end of the southwest monsoon or habagat, which was announced last October 5.

The northeast monsoon typically brings surges of cold temperatures, but the upcoming amihan period could be warmer as the existing strong El Niño in the tropical Pacific Ocean is predicted to become very strong in the fourth quarter of 2026. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Congress mourns LP stalwart, Martial Law survivor Raul Daza
articles.summary: Lawmakers on Monday mourned the passing of lifelong Liberal Party stalwart and former Northern Samar governor Raul Daza, who died last week at the age of 91.

blocks.text: Lawmakers on Monday mourned the passing of lifelong Liberal Party stalwart and former Northern Samar governor Raul Daza, who also represented the province at the House of Representatives at several times over the decades, including during the Martial Law regime and after the 1986 People Power revolution.

At the necrological service at the Batasang Pambansa, House Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez of South Cotabato called Daza a lifelong fighter for democracy. He recounted that Daza was a Liberal Party lawmaker who opposed President Ferdinand Marcos Sr.'s Martial Law regime, then became a Deputy Commissioner of the Presidential Commission on Good Government under the administration of President Corazon Aquino and a member of the House as Northern Samar Representative in the 8th, 9th, 10th, 15th, 16th, and 17th Congresses.

“In these capacities, he brought his extensive experience in legislation and governance closer to the communities whose welfare remained central to his life's work. He was steadfast in his principles, demonstrating a consistency of conviction that endured to the changing political circumstances and successive administrations,” Hernandez said.

“His legislative contributions reflected this conviction that the meaningful progress must be measured not simply by the laws enacted, by the opportunities they create and the lives they improved,” Hernandez added.

Some of the laws authored by Daza under Republic Act 6639, which renamed the Manila International Airport the Ninoy Aquino International Airport; Republic Act number 8291, or the Government Service Insurance System Act of 1997; and Republic Act 8544, which regulates the merchant marine profession in the Philippines.
Daza died on October 12 at the age of 91.

Former House Deputy Speaker Erin Tañada III also shared that while then-House Deputy Speaker Daza did oppose the passage of the Reproductive Health Law in Congress in 2012, a priority bill of President Benigno “Noynoy” Aquino III's administration, Daza did not use his position to delay the passage of the measure.

“Although he had his own convictions, he did not want to use his authority of the Speaker's gavel to obstruct the legislative process. He asked me to step in and preside whenever the bill was taken up. He didn't want to use the gavel to obstruct the legislative process. Think about the significance of that decision. Manong Raul did not abandon his principles,” Tañada said.

“He did not pretend to agree with something that conflicted with his own personal beliefs. He remained faithful to his convictions. But he also recognized that in a democracy, public service requires respect for institutions, for the legislative process, and for the legitimate will of the majority. He understood that holding a position of authority does not give us the right to use that authority to frustrate every decision with which we disagree,” he added.
Simple, meaningful gestures

House Deputy Minority Leader of Leila de Lima of ML party-list also recalled the times Daza paid her a visit during the times she was detained on drug charges where she was ultimately acquitted of, saying Daza faced the same persecution during the Marcos Martial law years.

“During my imprisonment, Manong Raul visited me in 2018 and also in 2019. He would occasionally send me books, letters, and rosaries. To some, this might seem like simple gestures, but to someone, for someone, whose freedom has been deprived of, that would come to understand, would understand how much, how much a familiar voice, a thoughtful letter, and a visit from an old friend can mean,” de Lima said.

“Manong Raul had known persecution himself. He lived through the dictatorship. He spent years in exile and returned to the Philippines despite the risk. I believe that experience gave him a particular understanding, what it meant to stand by someone during difficult times. And I will always be grateful that he stood by me,” she added.
Senator Risa Hontiveros, for her part, lauded Daza for standing up for what is right, no matter the costs and hearing out even those who are way younger than him.

“Manong Raul was a patriot who loved our country. He could have stayed in the United States where he had already won asylum [during the Marcos Martial Law era], but in the face of a standing warrant of arrest here, he chose to come back and fight. From a safer place, he moved back into the line of fire, getting arrested, being incarcerated, then joining the parliament of the streets and winning higher honor in our eyes,” Hontiveros said.

“An infinitely political animal, he sought the wise, even the purposes of such efforts, even from younger allies like me, in order to take his principal position on them as he had done at many other critical junctures of our nation's history. Raul Daza is a small boy who would not be bullied, who took up boxing to put muscle behind that resolve and who punched upward all throughout his life. He had a kind heart who gave as good as he got in the struggles of our times,” she added. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
articles.summary: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

image.caption: Anders Fernstedt has built a home outside one of London's most expensive propertiesImage: Dan Redding/DW

blocks.text: There's a lot of stopping and staring in Knightsbridge. This part of central London is within a stone's throw of Buckingham Palace, Hyde Park and Harrods, bringing inquisitive tourists in droves.

While it may not divert quite as many eyeballs as the seat of the British monarchy, a curious collection of plants, garden umbrellas, shopping bags and children's toys filling a building's entrance causes many a curious glance.
The peculiar arrangement on a grand portico is what Anders Fernstedt, a man from Sweden who fell on hard times, has been calling home for more than three years already.
That building hosting his makeshift setup was, just a few years ago, London's most expensive house.

The mega-mansion at 2-8A Rutland Gate sold in 2020 for a then-record £210 million (€244 million, $278 million) to Hui Ka Yan, the founder of China's Evergrande group, who was sentenced to life in prison last month.
Hui never moved in and the house was registered under his wife's name. The freezing of her assets means it can't be seized by liquidators and the house is in a state of limbo.
Chinese court hands Evergrande property tycoon life sentence
So too was Fernstedt when he first stumbled across it. "I just thought, it would be a shelter for the night. I'm an avid camper, like an amateur botanist. I'm not afraid of nature," he told DW.
'Camping on the balcony'

Fernstedt has never been inside the property, which appears to be in a state of disrepair. Instead, he gradually built his home in the portico, where grand columns guard the 45 rooms, indoor swimming pool and 116 windows. Year round he sleeps under the portico roof and a large umbrella which provides a hidden nook in which he's placed mattresses and bedding.
"I haven't had a bad night's sleep for as long as I can remember. And that goes for four seasons. It's not cold in the winter, and because I don't have walls, I get the breeze in the heat," he said.
"My conceit when I started was that sort of fake dream. Oh, I'm just a boy, my parents are in the house, everything's normal, I just asked them for permission to camp on the balcony."

blocks.caption: 2-8A Rutland Gate sold for €244 million in 2020 but has been unoccupied sinceImage: Dan Redding/DW

blocks.text: Fernstedt was raised by his mother in Sweden before embarking on a range of careers at home and in the US, building a name for himself in the tech world.
In 2016, he moved to England where he worked as a journalist and fact checker at publications including The Economist, before work dried up around the time of the COVID pandemic.

A share in a tech company from his days in the US gave Anders a nest egg he relied on. But it couldn't last forever and he found himself living in a tent and then temporary accommodation, where he experienced violence and brushed up against people with severe addictions.
"Perhaps in this contemporary world, the biggest curiosity about my lifestyle is I'm completely off money," he said.
Community support powers unusual lifestyle

Fernstedt has built relationships with bakeries, cafes and florists in which he gets unused food, flowers for his home and use of power. He also makes use of a homeless charity in nearby Victoria for showers, clothing donations and socializing. But he's also made himself a broadly accepted part of one of London's most affluent neighborhoods.

blocks.caption: Fernstedt's home evolved over several years, through donations and giftsImage: Dan Redding/DW

blocks.text: "This is a very sophisticated neighborhood. I'd stayed for a few weeks and I knew everybody knew that I was here. And I thought, how can I sort of convey my presence without being present? And I thought, my constituency has to be the neighbors' children and grandchildren. Because if they plead my case at the kitchen table, my prospects improve," he said, by way of explaining the toys that line his abode.

"It is, in a way, a squirrel's nut collection," he added, when asked if he's worried about leaving his possessions out in the open. "I have so many nuts that I won't notice when something disappears."

There are some neighbors who do object to his presence, but Anders does his best to keep his home neat and his life quiet. Indeed, many others feel his presence prevents the house being a target for thieves or vandals. Overall though, he's found the community welcoming.

"Sometimes they introduce themselves asking what might I want or need. And my stock answer being: 'well, what you just gave me, a little bit of normal time, right? And neighborly banter'," he said. "Sometimes I'll be given food and very elegant Italian dinner jackets and clothes have arrived on a few occasions."
Homelessness a growing concern in London

Not all homeless people in London have found such a stable lifestyle. Homeless charity Crisis estimates that there are over 200,000 people classified as homeless in England's capital, where "4,392 people were recorded sleeping rough in London between April and June, up from 4% on the same time last year. This is up 58% compared to 10 years ago."

According to government figures, there were 105,138 empty homes in London in 2025, or 1 in every 37 homes. Andy Burnham, who became British Prime Minister in July, has since vowed to offer "every rough sleeper in England a route off the streets by Christmas."
Britain's new PM takes on fight against homelessness
With such an enormous price tag, even after six years of being abandoned, Fernstedt knows that the house he lives at could potentially become untenable at virtually any moment.
But over the last few years, it's given him something he craved when pitching up his tent or being moved from one scary temporary residence to the next.
"I'm no longer really worried that I'll cycle around the corner and everything will be gone. Because I've been here so long, I'm free of worrying now, and if we worry too much, we won't be happy."

articles.title: AMLC: Manila court orders forfeiture of funds linked to terrorism financing
articles.summary: A Manila court has ordered the forfeiture of funds linked to terrorism financing, the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) said on Monday.

blocks.text: Published October 19, 2026 6:31pm
A Manila court has ordered the forfeiture of funds linked to terrorism financing, the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) said on Monday.

The AMLC said the Manila Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 18 ordered the forfeiture of P217,165 previously held in a bank account belonging to Abdulpatta Escalon Abubakar, who has been linked to terrorism financing activities.
“The successful forfeiture demonstrates the indispensable role of financial intelligence and asset recovery measures in disrupting terrorism financing,” the AMLC said in a statement.
“By depriving terrorist facilitators of access to funds and financial services, authorities can impede their ability to plan, support and sustain terrorist activities,"
The AMLC said that the forfeiture supposedly underscored the importance of financial investigations in the country’s efforts to combat terrorism financing.

According to the AMLC, law enforcement authorities had reported that Abubakar facilitated the transfer of funds from Saudi Arabia to the Philippines through the wives and relatives of members of the Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG).

It added that Abubakar had been designated as a terrorist under United Nations Security Council Resolution 1267 for allegedly acting as a facilitator for the Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIL).
The AMLC also said international authorities had identified Abubakar as a key facilitator who transferred US$50,000 to Isnilon Hapilon, a former ASG leader.

The funds were believed to have been used to acquire weapons and ammunition. Abubakar was also linked to efforts to procure materials for manufacturing improvised explosive devices, the AMLC said. — MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Greece: At least 12 die in migrant drownings overnight
articles.summary: Authorities say 12 people, including an infant, have drowned in Greek waters in two separate incidents overnight. Another 22 people were rescued. A search-and-rescue operation is ongoing.

image.caption: Thousands of migrants have drowned in Greek waters trying to reach Europe over the past 11 years [FILE]Image: Panagiotis Balaskas/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Greek Coast Guard officials say 12 migrants were killed in the Aegean Sea overnight in two separate boating accidents.

In the first incident, six people — four men, a woman and an infant — were killed in waters off the coast of Lesbos when "a speedboat carrying migrants collided with the port side of a police patrol vessel," according to the Coast Guard.
Eight people were reported rescued.
In the second incident, six people — five men and a woman — drowned after their boat capsized off the coast of Samos, while 14 were rescued.
A search-and-rescue mission is ongoing in the area.
Authorities say they arrested a 37-year-old Turkish national among the survivors in the first incident, identifying him ‌as ​a suspected smuggler and the operator of the speedboat.
Greece's Minister of Shipping and Island Policy Vassilis Kikilias blamed migrant traffickers for all of the deaths, posting on X, "Our position is non-negotiable: Zero tolerance for smugglers."
Turkey to Greece: Deadly migrant passage to Europe
Greece has long been a gateway ​to Europe for migrants and ⁠refugees from the Middle East, Africa and Asia who usually set off on the notoriously deadly sea voyage from Turkey.
According to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), refugee arrivals in Greece are declining this year.
As of October 11, 2026, some 25,000 arrivals had been recorded compared to 42,000 in 2025.
Almost one million migrants and refugees landed on Greece's shores during the 2015/2016 migration crisis, here, too, mainly from Turkey.

articles.title: Australian MP Helen Haines in critical condition after deliberate vehicle attack, prime minister says
articles.summary: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines was in a critical ‌condition on Monday after being deliberately struck by a car outside her office in Wangaratta, police and Prime ​Minister Anthony Albanese said.

image.caption: MP Helen Haines speaks to the media at Parliament House on Feb. 9 in Canberra, Australia. (Hilary Wardhaugh/Getty Images)

blocks.text: World·New
Australian lawmaker Helen Haines was in a critical ‌condition on Monday after being deliberately struck by a car outside her office in Wangaratta, police and Prime ​Minister Anthony Albanese said.
43-year-old driver arrested at the scene in Wangaratta in state of Victoria
Haines, 65, ‌was airlifted to hospital, Albanese said.
"This wasn't an accident. There was a deliberate act, it would appear. We don't know what the motivation is," Albanese told Australian Broadcasting Corp.
Victoria Police ​said a 43-year-old man had been arrested after the attack on the Independent MP in Wangaratta, around 200 kilometres northeast ⁠of Melbourne.
"A knife was located by police and seized from inside the Toyota," police said.
Victoria Police acting superintendent Ashley Mason told a news conference there was no further threat to the public.
Albanese ​said it was too early to determine the ⁠motive for the attack, though a terrorism taskforce ⁠would be investigating the arrested suspect.
"We thank ⁠the ⁠swift assistance ​of bystanders and the dedicated health workers who assisted ​her, and ⁠police for their response," a statement by Haines's family posted on her Facebook page said.
Haines was first elected to the Parliament in 2019 to represent the electoral division of Indi.
Prior to that, she spent three decades working in rural healthcare as a nurse, midwife and academic, completing a doctoral thesis at Sweden's Uppsala University on childbirth.
In Parliament,she has championed causes including climate change, regional housing and worked with the ruling Labour government to establish a National Anti-Corruption Commission.
"She's just a thoroughly decent, respectful human being who is a delight to work with, and her presence in the Parliament adds to it," said Albanese.
Authorities are concerned that there were more than 1,000 threats of violence against public figures in Australia in the past year and that being in public office has become more dangerous.

Australian Federal Police Commissioner Krissy Barrett said in 2025 that threats against parliamentarians had doubled over the past three years. Police data showed more than 1,000 such threats against politicians in the 2025-26 financial year, Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said Monday.

articles.title: Marcoleta suspended for 90 days over plunder charges
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan Third Division has ordered the preventive suspension of Sen. Rodante Marcoleta from his post as a senator due to plunder charges.

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 6:08pm
Senator Rodante Marcoleta boards a Philippine National Police coaster at the Sandiganbayan on Monday, July 6, 2026, upon his arrest over a plunder case.
The STAR / Michael Varcas
MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Third Division has ordered the preventive suspension of Sen. Rodante Marcoleta from his post as a senator due to plunder charges.
In a resolution penned by Justice Karl Miranda and promulgated on October 19, the anti-graft court ordered Marcoleta suspended for 90 days, effective upon his receipt of the resolution.
The suspension will automatically be lifted once the 90-day period expires, according to the anti-graft court.
The suspension stemmed from two separate cases filed against the lawmaker involving plunder and an alleged violation of Presidential Decree (P.D.) No. 46.

According to the charges, during his tenure as the SAGIP Party-List representative, Marcoleta allegedly amassed P75 million in ill-gotten wealth, which he did not declare in his Statement of Contributions and Expenditures.
He allegedly received the donations from his co-accused, former lawmaker Mike Defensor and businessman Aristotle Viray.

In its resolution, the anti-graft court explained that under Republic Act (R.A.) No. 7080, or the Plunder Law, and R.A. No. 3019, or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, preventive suspension is mandatory once a valid Information has been established.
The anti-graft court noted that there is no requirement for a pre-suspension hearing for plunder under its Internal Rules or existing jurisprudence.

“Considering that the Information has been determined to be valid, it becomes the ministerial duty of the Court to forthwith issue the order of preventive suspension. The Court has neither the discretion nor duty to determine whether or not a preventive suspension is required. There are no ifs and buts about it,” the anti-graft court said.

The anti-graft court maintained that a plain reading of the factual allegations in the Informations, if hypothetically admitted, sufficiently establishes the elements of plunder and violation of P.D. No. 46.
The Sandiganbayan also assured the public that Marcoleta's suspension will not disrupt the legislative branch.

“Moreover, the preventive suspension of Sen. Marcoleta will not affect the functions of the Senate. The Senate, a collegial body composed of 24 Senators, can still perform its functions even during the preventive suspension of a member. The Senate committees may also continue to perform their tasks through their remaining members,” the anti-graft court said.
On October 12, the anti-graft court also imposed a 90-day suspension on Sen. Jinggoy Estrada due to plunder charges.

articles.title: Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods
articles.summary:
Trudy weakens to tropical storm after warnings of strong winds and heavy rain, while one person killed in Greece

In contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, the Pacific has seen…
articles.byline: Alice Nightingale-Smith and Nick Lee for MetDesk

blocks.text: In contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, there has been ongoing activity in the Pacific, with Trudy being the 22nd and latest named system. The category 2 hurricane remained roughly 100 miles (160km) south-west of the coast of Mexico, meaning the worst of the conditions stayed offshore. However, the US National Hurricane Center put coastal parts of the states of Jalisco, Michoacán and Colima under hurricane warnings, with sustained winds of up to 60-90mph forecast on Sunday.

Rainfall totals of 100-150mm were likely for these areas, prompting warnings of flooding and landslides. Warnings also covered the risk of a dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves in areas of onshore winds across the coast of south-western Mexico. By Monday morning, Trudy had weakened and been downgraded to a tropical storm, with coastal warnings being lifted.

In Greece, heavy rain and thunderstorms caused severe flooding and one fatality across Rhodes, Evia and the Sporades islands last week. According to the National Observatory of Athens, a station in Rhodes recorded 202mm between 3.30am and 9.50am (UTC) on 14 October. Regional authorities reported more than 30 rescue and extrication operations in response to flooding, while the Greek coastguard said four passenger vehicles were swept into the sea during the storm. On Skiathos, flood waters swept away two cars.

blocks.caption: Cars swept into the sea on the Greek island of Rhodes. Photograph: Kyriakos Finas/Reuters

blocks.text: Five deaths were reported due to severe flooding in Istanbul, Turkey, last week. Heavy rain on 14 and 15 October prompted school closures, flight delays, disruptive flooding and landslides across several provinces. According to the Istanbul metropolitan municipality, 242mm of rain was recorded in Beykoz, a district of Istanbul province. Nearly 600 people were rescued after becoming stranded and at least 2,700 people were forced to evacuate their homes.

The Turkish state meteorological service issued further alerts for heavy rain and thunderstorms over the weekend across dozens of provinces, with at least an additional 40-60mm forecast for parts of the Marmara and western Black Sea regions.

articles.title: Marcos pushes to improve nurse-to-patient ratio in PH
articles.summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Monday underscored the need to improve the welfare of Filipino nurses, including by improving nurse-to-patient ratios and providing more opportunities for…

blocks.text: Published October 19, 2026 6:02pm

President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Monday underscored the need to improve the welfare of Filipino nurses, including by improving nurse-to-patient ratios and providing more opportunities for career growth.

Marcos made the statement at the Philippine Nurses Association Inc. (PNA) National Annual Convention 2026 in Pasay City, where he highlighted the contributions of Filipino nurses to the country and the global healthcare workforce.
“Your leaders and all the people that we talked to that are abroad speak of the hard work, the skill, and the dedication that our nurses offer and demonstrate wherever they go," Marcos said.
"I’m very proud to hear this because I know how much our nurses contribute to our country, but also to the countries where they serve,” he added.
The President said the contributions of Filipino nurses deserved the government’s recognition and a sustained commitment to improving their welfare and professional development.

“So, we work very, very hard to strengthen our healthcare system now. We must also work towards improving nurse-to-patient ratios, filling vacant positions, providing more opportunities for our Filipino nurses’ growth,” he said.
“All of this is necessary so that our nurses can carry out responsibilities more efficiently and ensure that our healthcare institutions better serve our people,” Marcos added.

He said his administration was working with the Department of Health (DOH), the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) and the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) to support nurses.
The President also cited the increase in funding for the Health Emergency Allowance, from P6.8 billion in 2022 to more than P110 billion in 2026, for public and private healthcare workers.

The government is also providing employment opportunities and review classes through the Clinical Care Associates Program for nursing graduates who have yet to pass the licensure examination, he said.

“Our goal is to help more qualified Filipinos enter the profession, strengthen the capabilities and protect the welfare of our nurses to ensure that our healthcare institutions have the workforce that they need to serve our communities,” Marcos said.
The President thanked nurses for their hard work and dedicated service.

“Ang inyong husay, ang inyong malasakit, dedikasyon ay patuloy na nagbibigay ng pag-asa sa ating mga kababayan, nagpapalakas sa ating sistemang pangkalusugan. Patuloy po kaming magsisikap upang maibigay ang suporta, benepisyo, at oportunidad na nararapat para sa inyo,” Marcos said.

(Your competence, compassion and dedication continue to give hope to our fellow Filipinos and strengthen our healthcare system. We will continue to strive to provide the support, benefits and opportunities that you deserve.)— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Ukraine got 'no warning' of Russian ballistic strikes, Zelenskyy says
articles.summary: Massive strikes overnight hit the capital Kyiv, and damaged power stations, killing at least one person and cutting power to hundreds of thousands.

image.caption: The strikes hit Kyiv, including this candy shop in the city centerImage: Efrem Lukatsky/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: A barrage of Russian ballistic miles struck Kyiv and the surrounding region on Monday, killing at least one person and knocking out power to over half a million homes, Ukrainian authorities said.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Telegram that Russia had launched 16 ballistic missiles, targeting Ukraine's energy facilities, 10 of which were hit, cutting power to some 550,000 households.
The president also lamented the lack of warning from Ukraine's international partners.
"Another Russian ballistic missile attack came in several waves overnight, and once again, there was no early warning from our partners," he wrote.

Ukraine's Air Force reported strikes, which included cruise missiles and drones, hitting 25 locations. Of the 269 recorded Shahed drones deployed in the overnight attack, Ukrainian air defenses reportedly downed or suppressed 243, as well as four missiles.
Ukraine strikes Putin's hometown, as Trump eases pressure on Russia
Moscow says it hit drone, missile hubs in Ukraine
Russia's Defense Ministry also confirmed the "massive strikes" on Monday, saying it had targeted Ukraine with "ground-based high-precision weapons and strike drones."

The ministry said it had hit a Ukrainian data center, a logistics hub storing components for drones and cruise missiles, a train depot storing missiles and an industrial facility involved in the production of drones.
It also said it had struck a bulk carrier in the Black Sea, some 130 kilometers (80 miles) from the port of Odesa, which the ministry said had been carrying military and dual-use cargo.

Ukraine did not confirm those targets but said that a medical facility had been hit in the capital, as well as one of the city's metro stations, according to a post by the Kyiv City Military Administration on Telegram.

blocks.caption: A police officer inspects the site of a fitness club that was hit by a missile Image: Valentyn Ogirenko/REUTERS

blocks.text: Kyiv, Washington disagree over pause to intelligence sharing
The overnight strikes come amid contradictory claims by both Ukraine and the US about pauses to intelligence sharing.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that Washington had not paused some of its intelligence sharing, denying a statement Zelenskyy made on Sunday.
"I don't know where [Zelenskyy's] getting these things ​or why he's saying these things to the press. You should go back and ask him. There's been no pause," Rubio said during a visit to Uzbekistan.
"What he should ​focus on, and what we want to be focused on, is bringing an end to this war. That's what he should be focused on," he added.
Ukraine is dependent on the ability of US intelligence to spot fast-moving ballistic missiles fired by Russia. Some recent attacks have taken place without warning, Ukrainian officials have reported.
How Trump is helping Putin

articles.title: US teens can access ‘nudify’ apps despite Apple and Google’s parental controls, report finds
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Using test accounts acting as 13-year-olds, Tech Transparency Project downloaded 135 apps with features to generate nonconsensual nude imagery

In December 2025, Morgan Dorfman…

blocks.text: In December 2025, Morgan Dorfman received distressing news: a student at her daughter’s Pennsylvania high school was making AI-generated pornographic material using the daughter’s image.
He was using an artificial intelligence image-editing app called Movely to create sexual videos from pictures of her daughter and five other girls.

What Dorfman’s daughter experienced is not an anomaly: students in high schools across the US are reporting similar cases. Their classmates are generating nonconsensual pornographic or nude imagery using so-called “nudify apps”.
Governments around the world have moved to ban these AI platforms from app stores, and most US states have implemented laws that criminalize possession of AI-generated child sexual abuse material.

However, in spite of regulations prohibiting them, nudification apps are still proliferating and remain accessible to teens, according to a report from the digital advocacy group Tech Transparency Project (TTP) shared exclusively with the Guardian and released on Monday.

TTP researchers created four test accounts, two Apple accounts and two Google accounts, indicating the account holders were 13 years old. They searched for image-editing or face-swapping apps using terms such as “AI video generator” or “adult AI”. Using these accounts for a purported 13-year-old, the researchers were able to download 135 apps with features enabling them to strip people of their clothes or swap their faces on to nude bodies. The researchers disrobed women in AI-generated images in their tests rather than using photographs of real women.
At the time of her daughter’s distress, Dorfman didn’t know it was possible to create pornographic material of an everyday person so easily.

“All the girls were very scared and confused about what to do next,” Dorfman said. “I knew what a deepfake was, but I thought it was like Taylor Swift and people using celebrities’ [images],” Dorfman said. “I didn’t know it was possible to take any picture or any screenshot of anybody that you have and do this.”

Dorfman, a mother of four, spent weeks trying to figure out how the app worked and compiling material to educate other parents. She downloaded Movely and was immediately prompted to create suggestive videos using any image. The free version promoted sexually suggestive templates including “clothes explosion”, “brassiere unfasten” and “underwear drop”, according to a demonstration Dorfman put together for parents that the Guardian reviewed. In the paid version, it became more explicit: she saw templates for the types of pornographic situations in which, according a classmate, her daughter had appeared.

Both Apple and Google prohibit these types of apps from being distributed on their platforms. The companies also will often age-gate apps with adult content, restricting or blocking minors’ access. However, TPP researchers found that the companies largely rely on the developers to determine whether their apps are appropriate for certain ages.

“Many nudify apps identified in the investigation were inaccurately rated as suitable for minors – meaning the teen users could access them even when parental controls were activated,” the report said.

Researchers found that one face-swapping app, which was advertised to them with an image of a woman performing oral sex, was rated appropriate for ages four and up. The free version of the app prompted users to superimpose real women’s faces on to templates of women in lingerie or, if users paid, in pornographic situations. The researchers were able to buy a subscription to the app from a 13-year-old’s account without an alert to a linked parental account.
Google said the company regularly takes “proactive steps to detect and remove apps with harmful content”.

“When violations are detected or reported to us, we investigate and take swift action, which in this case included suspending violating apps and restricting related search terms on our store,” Google spokesperson Dan Jackson said in a statement.

After TTP contacted Apple seeking comment on the findings of their study, Apple implemented changes that strengthened content moderation guidelines. The company now requires developers to preemptively prevent and remove nonconsensual intimate imagery including AI-generated images. Apple also said that the company reviews every app before it is published and that if a developer misrepresents any features, the company removes the app and its developers. The company said in addition to apps they already removed before the TTP report was shared with them, the company has also “taken action” on the remaining apps mentioned in the report.

“A number of the apps in this report are mainstream photo and video editing tools with legitimate, widely used functionality, and do not have nudification or deepfake capabilities,” said Apple spokesperson Adam Dema. “We prohibit nudify apps on the App Store, and remove developers who add capabilities like it after the App Review process – a malicious tactic known as bait-and-switch.”

Of the four accounts the researchers created, two were placed under parental controls that only allowed users to download apps marked suitable for 13-year-olds and only then with a parental signoff. However, the researchers found that neither Apple nor Google required or suggested parental signoff to acquire any of the nudification apps.
after newsletter promotion

One app, Image to Video Maker-Vidou AI, was rated appropriate for users aged nine and older. Upon opening the app, users were greeted by an image of a topless woman on a bus, according to the TTP study.
“The app had a feature that promised to digitally undress any person – and to demonstrate, it showed nude images of female celebrities,” the report read.

Age restrictions were also not entirely effective, the study found. In one case, when the researchers tried to download an adult-rated app from the Apple App Store, they came across a pop-up warning that the app contained “age-restricted material”. But all they had to do was confirm they were 17 or older, which Apple allowed the account to do despite its registered age being 13. The Google account without parental controls was blocked three times from downloading an age-restricted app but otherwise allowed the researchers to download nudification apps that were self-reported to be age-appropriate.

The Apple account that TTP set up parental controls for was still able to find and download 24 so-called “nudify” apps because they were all rated as appropriate for 13-year-olds. The Google account with parental controls was able to download 51 of these apps.

Removing image and video editing platforms from app stores was also not enough to prevent its use. In the course of TTP’s research, Apple took down 25 of the nudify apps, and Google took down six. However, the researchers were able to continue using the app since they had already downloaded it.

Dorfman had a similar experience with Movely, she said. While preparing a presentation for parents and law enforcement officials, she returned to the app and App Store to take screenshots when she realized it was no longer available to download. However, the app was already on her phone and it remained entirely functional. She was also still being charged for her paid subscription.
Once these nonconsensual images and videos are created, accountability proves evasive, Dorfman has found. “I just wanted someone to make him delete all of these videos,” she said.

In her daughter’s case, Dorfman feels her school has downplayed what happened. In a school-wide email the Guardian reviewed, the principal wrote that her daughter’s classmate did use the app to animate images of other students but that there was no evidence he had done anything inappropriate.
However, days later, Radnor police criminally charged him with harassment.

“The whole thing was dismissed as ‘it’s not real’,” Dorfman said. “The haunting trauma as a mom is that I can’t tell [my daughter] those videos are gone or who had them. We can’t search everyone’s phones, and he deleted the app.”

articles.title: [Rappler’s Best] And our jaws dropped
articles.summary: The impeachment court is on recess until November 9, when it’s the defense’s turn to present its case. What would the defense’s counter move be?

blocks.text: My apologies for missing last Monday’s newsletter as I took a short break.

This week is the start of the public interviews of five aspirants to the post of chief justice, which will be vacated by Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo on November 6. He is retiring after over five years since he was appointed by then-president Rodrigo Duterte.

It’s President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s first and only chance of choosing the head of the High Tribunal, which is packed with Duterte appointees, before he steps down in 2028. Two of the aspirants, Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen and Associate Justice Alfredo Benjamin Caguioa, were appointed to the Court by the late president Noynoy Aquino. The Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) will hold public interviews with both on Thursday, October 22.
The three other aspirants — Duterte appointees associate justices Rodil Zalameda, Japar Dimaampao, and Jose Midas Marquez — will be interviewed by the JBC on October 26.
With a Supreme Court in transition, we can’t expect it to rule on anything that could potentially shuffle the appointing power’s deck of cards.

Which is why, from a purely tactical point of view, it does make sense for the prosecution in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte to have made a bombshell bet last week — “all in,” in the words of lead prosecutor Jinky Luistro — by dropping all but one of the four articles of impeachment it lodged against her before the Senate impeachment court.

Unlike last year, when the Court saved the day for the Vice President by barring the first attempt to put her on trial, the defense could feel the winds shifting. “As for certiorari (before the Supreme Court), we are not considering it at this point,” said defense spokesperson Michael Poa in this story.

items: It’s the handwriting on the wall. In August, the SC dismissed two petitions, including one filed by Duterte herself, that questioned the impeachment proceedings against her, saying they were already moot since the trial had already proceeded.

A month later, Duterte lost the second time around, when the justices unanimously dismissed a petition against the Senate court’s decision to adjust the voting threshold to convict the Vice President.

On Day 39 of the trial last week, House prosecutors dropped three complaints against her — misuse of confidential funds, grave threats, and bribery — in a legal maneuver that upset the defense and made lead counsel Sheila Sison bristle with a staccato of qualms and unease. This should not tie our hands, she told the impeachment court.

The prosecution’s move partly stemmed from its reading of the defense’s strategy, which, they say, is to delay the proceedings and bore the public to death. Prosecutors believe they have gained momentum from their latest witness, accountant-lawyer Alex Cabrera, and wanted to go for the kill, so to speak.

Presiding officer Senator Chiz Escudero issued a quick decision that sided with the prosecution, thus retaining just one charge to be judged by the senator-judges: Duterte’s estimated P1.5-billion unexplained wealth, per Cabrera’s numbers.

Who benefits from this situation? In this story, political reporter Dwight de Leon tells us who, plus the fact that timing is already pretty tight, given the 2027 budget that needs to be passed and Manila’s hosting of the ASEAN Summit in mid-November.

blocks.text: For now, the impeachment court is on recess until November 9, when it’s the defense’s turn to present its case. What would the defense’s counter move be? Possibly two things, according to lawyer Lulu Reyes, Rappler’s resident panelist in our coverage of the trial. Watch it here.

items: The defense could seek an outright dismissal of all the articles of impeachment and no longer present its arguments, citing a mistrial.
It could file a demurrer to evidence with the impeachment court, a plea to dismiss the case because the prosecution failed to present sufficient evidence, i.e., Cabrera’s “false assumptions.”

blocks.text: Either way could force an early vote from the senator-judges, according to Reyes.
Truly a sui generis. Spin a win!

Shay Du tells us how the military’s structure has adapted to its plans to modernize.

Lourence Angelo Marcellana walks us through the armed forces’ modernization program. The latest proof of how the military is changing is the appointment of the first female officer to be the commandant of cadets at the Philippine Military Academy, as Mia Fokno writes in this story.
Eirene Manatlao looks into why Filipino women are opting out of motherhood. But can an aging Philippines avoid the fate of its neighbors? Read this report by Jake Gomez.
